Practice-relevant•FDA approval and prescribing information•April 30, 2026

FDA approves Auvelity for agitation associated with AD dementia

The April indication expansion adds a non-antipsychotic option for AD-related agitation; it is not an as-needed treatment.

Key quantitative results: In the label’s efficacy population, CMAI changed −14.9 with Auvelity (n=152) versus −11.6 with placebo (n=156); difference −3.3 points (95% CI −5.8 to −0.8) at week 5.

ManagementAgitation

Added September 7, 2026 · FDA action 2026-04-30; NCT03226522; NCT04947553

Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

The evidence supports symptom treatment, not slowing AD progression. Medication interactions and patient-specific risks remain important.

Study design

Five-week double-blind study in probable AD with moderate-to-severe agitation, MMSE 10–24; a separate withdrawal trial evaluated sustained responders.

Key quantitative results

  • In the label’s efficacy population, CMAI changed −14.9 with Auvelity (n=152) versus −11.6 with placebo (n=156); difference −3.3 points (95% CI −5.8 to −0.8) at week 5.
  • In the safety population, dizziness occurred in 9% of 159 treated patients versus 3% of 158 placebo patients; somnolence in 8% versus 4%.

What changed

FDA expanded a previously approved drug’s indication.

Strength of evidence

Regulator-confirmed efficacy; short-term symptom and responder-enriched maintenance designs.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

Adds an option for individualized agitation care.

Field medical relevance

Separate treatment benefit from class labels and mechanism.

Access or reimbursement relevance

Approval does not establish payer coverage or patient cost.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports
Can the withdrawal results predict benefit in every new patient?
No. The withdrawal study selected established responders.
Critique and limitationsBias, uncertainty, and missing evidence
  • No direct comparison with other approved agitation treatments.
  • Label warnings include suicidality, seizures, hypertension, serotonin syndrome and falls precautions; consult the full label.

Primary source · Prescribing information, sections 6.1 and 14.2
